History & Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old woman with a 3-day history of progressively worsening right-sided/global headache with photophobia and visual “shooting lights,” unrelieved by ibuprofen; clinical impression is an acute migraine-type headache.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe headache.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began ~3 days ago while at work; intensity has increased daily.  
• Location: Diffuse but maximal around the right eye.  
• Character: Constant dull ache with intermittent sharper pain; rated 8/10.  
• Fluctuation: Present continuously, with episodic surges in intensity.  
• Exacerbating factors: Bright light; possibly stress.  
• Relieving factors tried: Ibuprofen for 2 days (3 tablets/day) – minimal relief.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (“light hurts”), transient “shooting lights”; nausea without vomiting; difficulty concentrating.  
• Pertinent negatives: No visual loss or persistent blurring, no neck stiffness, no limb weakness, no speech difficulty, no fever, no rash, no recent head trauma.  
• Similar episodes: Occasional milder headaches relieved by ibuprofen; never this severe.  
• Ideas/concerns: Worried about developing migraines given family history.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior migraine diagnosis.

Medications:
• Ibuprofen – self-administered; dose/route/frequency not documented (pt reports 3 tablets/day).  
• No regular prescription medications.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with three housemates.  
• Occupation: IT professional; prolonged computer use.  
• Tobacco: Social smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social drinker.  
• Wears glasses since childhood; last eye exam not recent.

Family History:
• Mother and sister with recurrent migraines (mother more severe).

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General / HEENT / Neuro: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• None ordered or performed at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Acute severe headache most consistent with first-episode migraine without aura (photophobia, visual phenomena, family history, severity); tension headache less likely.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Migraine – supports: photophobia, “shooting lights,” moderate–severe unilateral-predominant pain, family history; opposes: patient denies prior migraines.  
2. Tension headache – supports: work stress, dull ache; opposes: high pain score, photophobia.  
No contradictory information between transcript and DDx.

Issue 1 – Acute severe headache (probable migraine):
• Provide adequate analgesia: advise ibuprofen 400 mg up to two tablets (max 3×/day) OR prescribe naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± paracetamol or codeine for breakthrough pain.  
• Educate on trigger avoidance; recommend reduced screen brightness, regular hydration, sleep hygiene.  
• Initiate headache diary to identify patterns/triggers.  
• Safety-net advice: return urgently for visual loss, focal weakness, speech difficulty, vomiting, fever, or worsening pain.  
• Follow-up: GP review in 1–2 weeks; earlier if escalation.

Issue 2 – Possible future migraine prophylaxis:
• Discussed that if headaches become recurrent/frequent, prophylactic agents can be considered at follow-up (e.g., beta-blockers, topiramate) – deferred today.

General Plan Items:
• Consider scheduling routine eye test due to longstanding glasses and possible eye-strain contribution.  
• Encourage smoking cessation and stress-management strategies.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No physical examination or vital signs documented; allergy status documented as “none,” but reconciliation of drug, food, environmental allergies could be expanded.  
• No objective neurological exam recorded despite headache presentation – recommend on follow-up.  
• Transcript contained clear audio; no major inaudible sections.
